title: Simple and compound interest: practice set
sourceNote: Original practice questions written for this group. None of them is a CAT previous-year question.
instructions: 10 questions, 20 minutes, CAT marking: +3 right, -1 wrong multiple choice, 0 for a wrong type-in answer.
Type-in answers take a number only: no %, ₹ or units. Use a decimal, not a fraction.

questions.text: What is the simple interest on ₹5,000 at 8% per annum for 3 years?
A sum of ₹6,000 grows to ₹7,080 in 3 years at simple interest. What is the rate of interest per annum (in %)?
What is the compound interest on ₹10,000 for 2 years at 10% per annum, compounded annually?
At simple interest, a sum of money doubles in 8 years. What is the rate per annum (in %)?
What is the difference between the compound interest (compounded annually) and the simple interest on ₹20,000 for 2 years at 5% per annum?
₹16,000 is invested for 1 year at 20% per annum, compounded half-yearly. What is the compound interest earned (in ₹)?
A sum invested at 5% per annum, compounded annually, amounts to ₹4,410 after 2 years. What was the sum invested?
Rohan borrows a sum at 10% per annum, compounded annually, and repays it in two equal annual instalments of ₹1,210 each. The first is paid at the end of year 1. What sum did he borrow?
The difference between the compound interest (compounded annually) and the simple interest on a sum for 3 years at 10% per annum is ₹465. What is the sum?

₹41,000 is split into two parts. One part is lent at 10% per annum simple interest and the other at 10% per annum compound interest, compounded annually. After 2 years the interest earned on the two parts is equal. What is the part lent at compound interest (in ₹)?
